paragraphs.title: Israel Gathers and the Crime Is Presented

easy.explanation: Israel gathered together unto the Lord in Mizpeh.
easy.q: Where did all the children of Israel gather?

easy.explanation: Four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword were present.
easy.q: How many footmen that drew sword were numbered among Israel?

easy.explanation: The Levite, the husband of the slain woman, gave the testimony.
easy.q: Who told Israel what had happened at Gibeah?

answers: To understand the wickedness and seek counsel
medium.explanation: They asked, “how was this wickedness?” and then requested advice and counsel.
medium.q: Why did the children of Israel ask the Levite to tell them what had happened?

answers: Give guidance about what should be done
medium.explanation: The people wanted counsel about how to respond.
medium.q: What does “give here your advice and counsel” mean?

answers: The testimony, the gathering, and the request for counsel
The gathering, the testimony, and the request for counsel
The request for counsel, the battle, and the testimony
medium.explanation: Israel gathered, heard the Levite, and then asked for advice.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the opening of the chapter?

answers: The tribes acted as a united assembly
The people scattered among the cities
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes their unity and common purpose.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “as one man” emphasize about Israel’s gathering?

answers: To show all Israel the wickedness committed at Gibeah
To find a place to live
To recruit the seven hundred slingers
challenge.explanation: He sent the pieces throughout the land to display the outrage committed in Israel.
challenge.q: Why did the Levite cut his concubine in pieces and send them throughout Israel?

challenge.explanation: He said that the men had committed “lewdness and folly in Israel.”
challenge.q: Which word in the Levite’s testimony expresses a serious moral judgment?

paragraphs.title: The Decision for War and Tribal Mobilization

easy.explanation: They determined to go up by lot against Gibeah.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel decide to do to Gibeah?

answers: The surrender of the guilty men
easy.explanation: They demanded that Benjamin deliver the men of Belial from Gibeah.
easy.q: What did Israel demand from Benjamin?

easy.explanation: The Lord answered, “Judah shall go up first.”
easy.q: Which tribe was appointed to go up first?

answers: Benjamin refused to deliver the guilty men
Benjamin asked to lead all Israel
medium.explanation: Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of the other tribes.
medium.q: Why did conflict develop between Israel and Benjamin?

answers: They carried or used swords for battle
medium.explanation: The expression identifies men prepared for warfare.
medium.q: What does “drew sword” mean in this passage?

answers: Israel had a much larger army
Benjamin had a much larger army
Both sides had only seven hundred men
medium.explanation: Israel had four hundred thousand men, while Benjamin had twenty-six thousand plus seven hundred chosen men.
medium.q: What do the numbers show about the armies?

answers: A desire to avoid every decision
challenge.explanation: They agreed to remain united until action had been taken.
challenge.q: What does Israel’s decision not to return to his tent show?

answers: They were lefthanded slingers who could hit an hair breadth
challenge.explanation: Every one was lefthanded and could sling stones accurately without missing.
challenge.q: What special ability is mentioned concerning seven hundred Benjamite men?

answers: The refusal turned the dispute into a military confrontation
The refusal caused Israel to join Benjamin
challenge.explanation: Benjamin defended Gibeah instead of surrendering the guilty men, so both sides prepared for battle.
challenge.q: How did Benjamin’s refusal lead to war?

easy.explanation: The Lord had said, “Judah shall go up first.”
easy.q: Who was to go up first in the battle?

easy.explanation: Benjamin destroyed down to the ground twenty and two thousand Israelites.
easy.q: How many Israelites were killed on the first day?

easy.explanation: Benjamin destroyed another eighteen thousand Israelites.
easy.q: What happened on the second day?

answers: They encouraged themselves and arranged the battle again
They accepted Benjamin’s offer of peace
medium.explanation: The people encouraged themselves and set their battle again in array.
medium.q: What did the Israelites do after the first defeat?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the Israelites being killed in battle.
medium.q: In this context, what does “down to the ground” describe?

answers: Israel asked the Lord and was nevertheless defeated
medium.explanation: Israel consulted the Lord before both attacks, yet Benjamin prevailed.
medium.q: What was similar about the first two defeats?

answers: Permission to fight did not guarantee immediate victory
There was no need to ask the Lord
Benjamin did not participate in the battle
challenge.explanation: Israel received direction to go up, but still suffered two defeats.
challenge.q: What may the sequence of defeats teach about asking whether to fight?

challenge.explanation: Twenty-two thousand plus eighteen thousand equals forty thousand.
challenge.q: How many Israelites fell during the first two days together?

answers: They still regarded Benjamin as part of Israel
challenge.explanation: Even during the conflict, Israel called Benjamin their brother.
challenge.q: What does Israel’s use of the word “brother” show?

easy.explanation: All Israel went up and came unto the house of God.
easy.q: Where did Israel go after the first two defeats?

answers: They wept, fasted, and offered sacrifices
They sent the ark into the wilderness
easy.explanation: They wept, fasted until evening, and offered burnt and peace offerings.
easy.q: What did Israel do at the house of God?

easy.explanation: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, stood before the Lord.
easy.q: Who stood before the Lord when Israel asked again?

answers: They wept, fasted, and offered sacrifices
medium.explanation: Their renewed inquiry was accompanied by weeping, fasting, and offerings.
medium.q: What did Israel do before asking the Lord again?

answers: A signal rising from the city
A weapon carried by the army
medium.explanation: The flame and smoke served as a sign connected with the ambush and capture of Gibeah.
medium.q: In this battle context, what was the “flame with smoke” used for?

answers: Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver them into thine hand
medium.explanation: The Lord promised, “to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand.”
medium.q: What answer did the Lord give Phinehas?

answers: Israel added weeping, fasting, and offerings
challenge.explanation: The third inquiry followed a deeper expression of repentance and dependence.
challenge.q: What major change occurred before Israel’s third inquiry?

answers: The inquiry took place in the presence of the covenant symbol
The ark had been taken by Benjamin
The ark was used as a weapon
challenge.explanation: The text says that the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days.
challenge.q: What does the mention of the ark of the covenant show?

answers: It gave Israel confidence to make a third attack
It caused Israel to abandon the ambush
It removed the need for an army
challenge.explanation: After receiving the promise of victory, Israel went up and prepared the ambush.
challenge.q: How did the Lord’s promise affect the next battle plan?

paragraphs.title: The Stratagem and the Turning of the Battle

easy.explanation: Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah.
easy.q: What did Israel set around Gibeah?

easy.explanation: A great flame with smoke rose out of the city.
easy.q: What sign showed that the city had been captured?

easy.explanation: The Lord smote Benjamin before Israel.
easy.q: What finally happened to the Benjamites?

answers: They fled and caused Benjamin to pursue them
medium.explanation: Israel gave place and drew Benjamin from the city toward the highways.
medium.q: How did Israel draw the Benjamites away from Gibeah?

answers: A force hiding and waiting to surprise an enemy
medium.explanation: The ambush forces hid until the appointed time and then attacked.

answers: They saw Israel retreating and struck them
They heard that the battle was over
medium.explanation: They believed Israel was being smitten down as in the first battle.
medium.q: Why did the Benjamites initially think they were winning?

answers: It was an arranged signal that the battle had turned
It merely hid the Israelite army
challenge.explanation: The smoke signaled that the ambush had entered the city and the battle had changed.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the smoke in Israel’s plan?

answers: They saw the flame of the city ascend to heaven
They received an order from Israel
challenge.explanation: When they looked behind them and saw the city burning, they knew evil had come upon them.
challenge.q: What made the Benjamites realize that the situation had changed?

answers: The city became a wilderness without a battle
challenge.explanation: Benjamin first pursued Israel, but after the ambush Israel pursued Benjamin.
challenge.q: What reversal occurred in the third battle?

paragraphs.title: The Pursuit and Destruction of Benjamin’s Towns

easy.explanation: They turned their backs toward the way of the wilderness.
easy.q: Toward where did the Benjamites flee?

easy.explanation: Six hundred men fled to the rock of Rimmon.
easy.q: How many Benjamites survived at the rock of Rimmon?

easy.explanation: Israel set on fire all the cities that they came to.
easy.q: What did Israel do to the cities of Benjamin?

answers: Benjamin fled, and many of its men were killed
medium.explanation: The Benjamites fled, while Israel destroyed many of them on the roads and in the cities.
medium.q: What happened during the pursuit after Gibeah fell?

answers: They chased them continually and closely
They gave them a place to rest
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a determined and relentless pursuit.
medium.q: What does “pursued hard after them” mean?

answers: Eighteen thousand plus five thousand plus two thousand
Five thousand plus six hundred only
medium.explanation: The passage lists eighteen thousand, five thousand, and two thousand slain.
medium.q: Which calculation matches the casualties listed for Benjamin that day?

answers: They escaped to the rock of Rimmon and remained there four months
They were only the men of Gibeah
challenge.explanation: Six hundred men fled to Rimmon and abode there four months.
challenge.q: What distinguished the six hundred survivors from the rest of Benjamin?

answers: The destruction reached Benjamin’s cities, not only Gibeah
The battle ended immediately at Gibeah
Only seven hundred men were involved
challenge.explanation: Israel struck the men, cities, beasts, and all that came to hand throughout Benjamin.
challenge.q: What does the end of the chapter show about the extent of the conflict?

answers: Pursuit, flight to Rimmon, four months there, and destruction of the cities
Destruction of the cities, pursuit, flight, and four months at Rimmon
Four months at Rimmon, a Benjamite victory, and destruction of the cities
challenge.explanation: The Benjamites were pursued, six hundred escaped to Rimmon, and the cities were then destroyed.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the end of the war?
